phase3_findings.description: docs/external/release-notes.md has no entry for this change. The first '## Unreleased' section, directly below the October 28, 2026 entry, mentions neither save_text_memories nor the agent no longer saving free-form notes. Acceptance criterion four requires an entry there stating the agent no longer saves free-form notes unless save_text_memories = true, marking it a behavior change for existing deployments, telling TOML and environment-variable operators to set save_text_memories = true to keep the old behavior, telling MCPB users to tick the new checkbox, and explaining that earlier notes stay in memory and are still used, that an agent-written note cannot be told apart from an imported one, that TOML and environment operators can review and delete wrong notes with the memory-administration tools, linking the 'Memory-Administration Tools for the Assistant' section of docs/external/managing-memory.md, and that an MCPB install's settings cannot turn those tools on.

The expanded comment runs eight lines, of which only the last three name a wrong change and its consequence (do not move the gate into SaveTextMemoryTool.execute or ChromaAgentMemory.save_text_memory, which would drop curated notes). The earlier lines restate what save_text_memory is for and how has_text_memory gates the prompt section, already recorded in docs/internal/agent/memory.md. The comment is accurate, just longer than the project standard asks.

With the tool unregistered, a model that still emits a save_text_memory call receives the registry's "Tool 'save_text_memory' not found" card, which can turn an otherwise successful query_database answer into an error result for the MCP client. The change adds no handling or test for that path. The failure is loud rather than silent and the prompt section is now dropped, so the trigger is unlikely.

No test composes the environment-variable arm of acceptance criterion three end to end. tests/unit/test_config_schema.py lines 317 to 322 prove the environment variable sets the field and tests/unit/test_factory_wiring.py lines 479 to 491 prove a true field registers the tool, but nothing runs Config.load under SQLLENS_MEMORY__SAVE_TEXT_MEMORIES and then build_agent. The gate reads cfg.memory.save_text_memories directly, so the escape risk is low.

The mcpb/README.md settings row acceptance criterion two requires has no assertion, unlike the manifest field, its environment mapping and the deliberate absence of allow_admin_tools and insecure, which the new test pins. Since no pull-request job builds the bundle, a later manifest title or default change can drift from the published table unnoticed. The consequence is limited to documentation.

## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (one acceptance criterion unmet in documentation only)

The code change is correct and well covered by tests, but one acceptance criterion asks for a release-note entry that this branch does not have, so a reviewer should add that entry before merge rather than treat the PR as finished.

Rule applied: rule 6 — a finding and a checklist FAIL below the threshold remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `docs/external/release-notes.md` has no entry for this change. The first `## Unreleased` section, the one directly below the October 28, 2026 entry, lists entries on profile names, metadata, SQL checks, dependencies, memory import, model info, labels and one-row answers, and none of them mentions `save_text_memories` or says that the agent no longer saves free-form notes. Acceptance criterion four asks this section for a specific entry: that the agent no longer saves free-form notes unless `save_text_memories = true`, that this is a behavior change for existing deployments, how an operator who uses a TOML file or environment variables restores the old behavior, how an MCPB user restores it with the new checkbox, that notes saved earlier stay in memory and are still used, that a note the agent wrote cannot be told apart from an imported one, that a TOML or environment operator can review and delete wrong notes with the memory-administration tools, with a link to the "Memory-Administration Tools for the Assistant" section of `docs/external/managing-memory.md`, and that an MCPB install's settings cannot turn those tools on. A deployment that upgrades and relied on agent-written notes stops writing them with nothing in the release notes to explain why. The required entry (behavior change, TOML/env/MCPB instructions, link to managing-memory.md#memory-administration-tools-for-the-assistant) is absent.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (4)

<details><summary>4 items</summary>

1. `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py` lines 132 to 140 carry an eight-line comment of which only the last three lines name a wrong change and its consequence, namely that the gate must not move into `SaveTextMemoryTool.execute` or `ChromaAgentMemory.save_text_memory` because that would drop curated notes. The earlier lines restate what `save_text_memory` is for and how `has_text_memory` gates the prompt section, which `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` already records. The comment is accurate, just longer than the project's standard asks for. (raised by 1/5 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py` lines 143 to 144 leave one residual error path. With the tool unregistered, a model that still asks for `save_text_memory` gets the tool registry's "Tool 'save_text_memory' not found" card, which can turn an otherwise successful `query_database` answer into an error result for the MCP client. The change adds no handling or test for that path. The failure is loud rather than silent, and the prompt section is now dropped, so the trigger is unlikely. (raised by 1/5 agents)
3. No test composes the environment-variable path end to end. Acceptance criterion three names two arms, `save_text_memories = true` in TOML and `SQLLENS_MEMORY__SAVE_TEXT_MEMORIES=true` with no TOML key, each reaching a registered `SaveTextMemoryTool` and the "TEXT MEMORY" prompt section. The tests split that: `tests/unit/test_config_schema.py` lines 317 to 322 prove the environment variable sets the field, and `tests/unit/test_factory_wiring.py` lines 479 to 491 prove a true field registers the tool, but nothing runs `Config.load` under the environment variable and then `build_agent`. The gate reads `cfg.memory.save_text_memories` directly, so the escape risk is low. (raised by 1/5 agents)
4. `mcpb/README.md`'s settings row has no test pinning it, unlike the manifest. `tests/unit/test_mcpb_manifest.py` pins the manifest field, its environment mapping and the deliberate absence of `allow_admin_tools` and `insecure`, which matters because no pull-request job builds the bundle. The matching README row that acceptance criterion two asks for has no assertion, so a later manifest title or default change can drift away from the published table without any test noticing. The consequence is limited to documentation. (raised by 1/5 agents)

</details>
